title: Week 2: The Undefeated Four and the Winless Four
synopsis: Week 2 draws the battle lines as Lickety Splitz Squad and Prestige Worldwide claim the top two spots while Love Hurts and three others sink to 0-2, plus Devin Lloyd drops 41.5 points and DJ Moore goes negative.
script:
Ladies and gentlemen, football fanatics and fantasy degenerates, THIS is THE NUTCAST, your weekly deep dive into the beautiful chaos of the NUT Fantasy Football League, where The Iron Throne awaits the worthy and the Toilet Bowl haunts the weak. I'm Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan, and brother, Week 2 just separated the contenders from the pretenders in a hurry.

We've got four teams sitting pretty at 2-0, four teams drowning at 0-2, and the rest fighting for their lives in the middle. Let's break it down.

First, your new number one in the Power Rankings: Lickety Splitz Squad. Twillie391 just hung 241.04 points on JSN Your Face, the highest score of the week by a country mile. Josh Allen out of Buffalo went absolutely nuclear with 40.82 points, slinging it like his life depended on it. Ja'Marr Chase chipped in 23. That's what we call a statement victory, folks. Lickety Splitz moves to 2-0, claims the top spot in both the standings and the Power Rankings with a 94.7 composite score, and they are the hottest team in the league right now.

But don't sleep on Prestige Worldwide. Cincy kid is also 2-0 after absolutely demolishing Love Hurts by 96.4 points, the biggest blowout of Week 2. Jonathan Taylor rumbled for 27.2, Dallas Turner the rookie linebacker out of Minnesota dropped 22, and Prestige Worldwide rolled to 233.74. That 96-point beatdown is the kind of statement that makes opponents check the schedule with dread. Prestige sits at number two in the Power Rankings with an 83.9 score, and they look every bit the part.

Now let's talk about the league's top individual performances, because Week 2 gave us some absolute monsters. Number one on the leaderboard: Devin Lloyd, linebacker for Carolina, rostered by The OG Champ. 41.5 points. Forty-one-and-a-half. Lloyd was an absolute wrecking ball, and that performance helped The OG Champ bounce back from a Week 1 loss by crushing Breece & Desist 232.49 to 161.71. Davante Adams added 37 points in a Rams uniform, Dak Prescott threw for 29.76, and just like that, The OG Champ rockets from twelfth in the standings to sixth. That's how you respond to adversity, folks.

Josh Allen's 40.82 was the second-best performance of the week. Third best? Jaxon Smith-Njigba with 38 points for JSN Your Face, and here's the tragedy: it wasn't even close to enough. JSN Your Face drops to 0-2 despite JSN himself going absolutely bonkers. That's fantasy football, folks. You can get a 38-burger from your namesake receiver and still lose by 81 points.

Rounding out the top performances: Davante Adams at 37, CeeDee Lamb with 31.3 for White Center Rats, and Amon-Ra St. Brown with 30.7 for Price is wrong BItch. The studs were studding in Week 2.

But let's talk about the other side of the coin. DJ Moore out of Buffalo, rostered by The Many-Faced Squad, put up negative 0.1 points. That's not a typo. Negative. You actually lost points by starting DJ Moore this week. Malik Nabers managed just 0.6 for Price is wrong BItch. Colston Loveland, the rookie tight end out of Chicago, gave Love Hurts exactly 0.8 points. Jayden Reed scraped together 0.9 for Breece & Desist. Those are the kinds of performances that haunt your dreams and tank your week.

The closest game of the week came down to Boom Goes The Dynamite edging Gus Swayze's Squad 162.87 to 143.05, a margin of just 19.8 points. Greg Rousseau with 24.5 and Nakobe Dean with 20.75 carried Boom to 2-0, even though they slipped from first to third in the Power Rankings. Meanwhile, Gus Swayze falls to 0-2 despite Travis Kelce dropping 20.6. Sometimes the veteran can't save you.

Let's talk Power Rankings movement because we had some seismic shifts. White Center Rats jumped from fifth to third after demolishing Points Against Champion 210.32 to 144.37. CeeDee Lamb, Jared Goff with nearly 30, and Budda Baker with 22 points powered that victory. The Many-Faced Squad stays undefeated at 2-0 but slips from tenth to sixth in the Power Rankings after beating Price is wrong BItch 192.03 to 148.97. Brock Purdy threw for 28.48, but that DJ Moore goose egg probably cost them some style points.

And then there's the 0-2 club. Love Hurts is dead last at twelve after getting blown out. Gus Swayze's Squad sits at eleven. JSN Your Face at nine and Breece & Desist at ten are both winless, and Breece & Desist took the biggest tumble in the Power Rankings, plummeting from third to ninth after back-to-back losses. When Jayden Reed gives you 0.9 points, you're not winning many matchups.

The Iron Throne is a long way off, folks, but Week 2 showed us who's got the firepower and who's got the holes. Lickety Splitz Squad and Prestige Worldwide look like juggernauts. The OG Champ made a statement. And four teams are staring down the barrel of an 0-2 start wondering where it all went wrong.

That's the week that was in the NUT Fantasy Football League. I'm Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan reminding you: in dynasty, every week writes a new chapter, and this one was written in blowouts, breakouts, and bruised egos. Until next week, keep your lineups tight and your FAAB bids tighter. This is THE NUTCAST.

title: Week 1: Boom Goes the Dynamite Explodes
synopsis: The 2026 NUT Fantasy Football League kicks off with fireworks as Boom Goes The Dynamite drops a season-high 252.9 to rocket from dead last to first place, while underdogs bite back and The OG Champ stumbles out of the gate.
script:
Good morning, good afternoon, good evening, wherever you are in NUT Nation -- this is Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan, and you are locked in to THE NUTCAST, your weekly audio destination for everything that matters in The NUT Fantasy Football League! We are LIVE for Week 1 of the 2026 season, and folks, if this opening salvo is any indication, we are in for one absolutely electric campaign. Six matchups in the books, twelve teams battling for glory and the Iron Throne, and let me tell you, the first cut is the deepest. Let's crack some shells and see who came to play!

We start at the very top of the leaderboard, where brandishrewsberry and Boom Goes The Dynamite just detonated the scoreboard. Two hundred and fifty-two point nine. Say it with me: two fifty-two point nine! That is not just the week's high score, that is a statement of intent. Boom came into Sunday ranked twelfth in the preseason standings, dead last, but after absolutely torching White Center Rats by 23.7 points, they've launched eleven spots straight to number one. Greg Rousseau on defense put up 32.5, a defensive lineman giving you thirty-two and a half in Week 1, that is house money right there. White Center Rats, by the way, didn't go quietly -- they posted 229.25 behind Derrick Henry's 34.8 and D'Andre Swift's 31.9, and they still took the L. That's dynasty football, folks. Sometimes you bring a cannon to a gunfight and the other guy brought a missile.

Now let's talk about the week's biggest blowout, because twillie391 and the Lickety Splitz Squad put on an absolute clinic. They hung 239.77 on Love Hurts, winning by 87.4 points. Eighty-seven point four! That is not a margin of victory, that is a restraining order. Josh Allen went for 35.66, T.J. Watt put up 34.5, Christian Watson chipped in 29.7, and by the time the dust settled, Love Hurts was limping off the field at 152.35. Lickety Splitz jumped three spots in the standings and now sit at number two. The scary part? They had Kyle Pitts put up a goose egg and still won by nearly ninety. When you can afford a zero from your tight end and still drop 240, you are not a team, you are a problem.

On the flip side, let's pour one out for The OG Champ. JeffPeterson20's squad posted the week's lowest score at 134.6, falling to Price is wrong BItch by 36.3. The OG Champ dropped six spots from sixth to twelfth, and when you're staring at the bottom of the standings in Week 1, you're already eyeing that Toilet Bowl. Jacob Saylors gave you zero. Zero! You can't win in this league when your running back forgets to show up. Price is wrong BItch, meanwhile, rode Jahmyr Gibbs for 31.1 and Amon-Ra St. Brown for 23.7, climbing five spots to sixth. Smittytribe27 is smiling tonight.

Closest game of the week came down to single digits. Prestige Worldwide edged JSN Your Face 223.61 to 214.88, a margin of just 8.7 points. Kenneth Walker put up 32.6 for Prestige, Trevor Lawrence added 26.1, Jonathan Taylor chipped in 23.6, and cincy_kid walked away with the win. BillsMafia1480 had to watch his squad drop seven spots in the standings despite posting 214. That is the cruelest part of fantasy football -- you can score 214 and still lose. You can do everything right and still go home empty.

Now, the upset of the week, the one time the betting line got embarrassed. Breece & Desist came in as a 5.5-point favorite over The Many-Faced Squad, and CamWells16 said not today. The Many-Faced Squad won 215.68 to 193.31, a 22.4-point upset fueled by Bijan Robinson's 27.3 and linebacker Ventrell Miller's 24.25. Awesomeus got a nice game from Bryce Young, 32.44, but when Kyler Murray gives you 0.62, you are cooked. The Many-Faced Squad climbed five spots to fourth, Breece & Desist dropped seven to ninth, and the bookies are licking their wounds.

League-wide standout performances -- Caleb Williams led all scorers with 37.26 for Points Against Champion. The rookie signal-caller is here to play. Josh Allen, Derrick Henry, T.J. Watt, Kenneth Walker, Greg Rousseau, all north of thirty-two points. The league is loaded with talent, and Week 1 showed it.

On the bust side, we had four players put up absolute zeroes: Kyle Pitts, Colston Loveland, Jacob Saylors, and Myles Garrett. Myles Garrett, folks. A defensive end capable of wrecking a game, and he gave Price is wrong BItch a bagel. Somehow they still won. That is the beauty and the brutality of this game.

Power Rankings after Week 1 have Lickety Splitz Squad at number one with a score of 78.1. Prestige Worldwide sits second at 63.1. Breece & Desist dropped to third despite the loss because the algorithm still respects the roster. Points Against Champion, ironically, fell to twelfth in the Power Rankings despite winning their matchup. The numbers never lie, but sometimes they do raise an eyebrow.

Week 1 is in the books. Six winners, six losers, and a whole lot of storylines brewing. The road to the Iron Throne is long, the Toilet Bowl looms for the unlucky, and every week the league bank is watching, waiting to collect those trade and waiver taxes. This is The NUT Fantasy Football League, and this is your Nutcast. I'm Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan, reminding you: stay sharp, stay hungry, and never, ever trust a tight end named Kyle. We'll see you next week!
